title: Runtime patch and mitigation for KV state corruption and spike OOMs in long-tail production workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported transient production failures over the past two weeks. Symptoms included sudden spike GPU OOMs during long-running chat sessions, degraded throughput, and in a subset of cases corrupted model outputs traced to inconsistent KV cache state. Investigation indicates a race between the async KV serialization/replication path and the runtime's slab allocator compaction routine when servicing very long-tail sequence histories and frequent autoscaling-driven worker churn. This produced two correlated issues: (1) stale / partially-written KV frames (manifesting as deserialization errors and token misalignment in downstream decode), and (2) increased memory fragmentation leading to small, frequent OOMs on GPUs with tight headroom.

Impact: High. Three paying customers experienced user-facing outages (latency spikes >10s, generation failures) and one Dedicated customer required capacity failover. Affected model families: quantized LLaMA variants and one custom 30B derivative. Affected modes: streaming generation with large context windows and frequent prefix cache invalidations.

Root cause (short): Race in KV write path + allocator compaction. When autoscaler removed or rolled workers during heavy long-context sessions, in-flight KV writes could be observed by a concurrent compaction pass that performed in-place pointer reshuffling leading to partial writes. On quantized attention caches the partial writes appeared as invalid cache entries, causing decoder to request expanded GPU allocations, which in turn triggered fragmentation-sensitive OOMs. The allocator also lacked a defensive fallback when allocation requests failed on a fragmented device.

Proposed fix: 1) Add atomic swap semantics to KV write: write to a staging blob and atomically replace the active reference. 2) Add CRC/version validation to KV frames and explicit rejection/fallback when corruption detected. 3) Introduce a lightweight defragmentation pass triggered on allocation failures for GPU pools that support it, plus conservative allocator tuning to avoid worst-case fragmentation (reduce minimum slab size for runtimes using quantized models). 4) Short-term mitigation: force synchronous KV persistence for Dedicated/Private customers with autoscaler churn > 20% to avoid races, and enable a temporary config that disables aggressive compaction while the hotfix is rolled out.

Rollout plan: Patch branch runtime/pin-atomic-kv-16420 -> run unit + integration tests -> dogfood on canary fleet for Hosted (10% traffic) -> enable for affected Dedicated customers via per-tenant flag -> offer on Private as opt-in package. Expect full rollout to all Hosted by 2025-02-20 subject to canary stability.

Verification: Add end-to-end test that simulates worker churn with long-context sequences and checks KV checksum invariants. Add Datadog monitors: KV-write-error-rate, KV-repair-count, device-fragmentation-score, and per-tenant OOM spikes. Post-deploy, monitor for 72 hours with SLO alert thresholds halved for early detection.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Aisha Patel: Initial customer escalation opened after Customer A (Dedicated) reported repeated generation failures during long-chat ingest. Collected logs and core dumps; linked artifacts below. Marking as P0 due to customer SLA impact.

2025-02-11 — Maya Chen (SRE): Observed correlated OOM spikes in Datadog on GPU pool 'dedicated-eu-central-7' aligned with autoscaler-scale-in events. Captured a sample of allocator debug traces; fragmentation metric steadily rising prior to OOM.

2025-02-12 — Diego Ramirez: Reproduced in a private repro by simulating worker churn while running 50 concurrent long-context streams. Verified token misalignment reproduces when a KV write overlaps compaction. Created failing unit test 'KVAtomicitySpec'.

2025-02-13 — Connor Lee (Reviewer): Reviewed PR attempt that added mutex around KV write. Suggested avoiding coarse locks to prevent latency regressions; recommended staging-blob + atomic pointer swap approach instead. Also requested CRC/version validation for safety.

2025-02-14 — Diego Ramirez: Implemented staging blob + atomic swap + CRC check in runtime branch 'bugfix/kv-atomic-swap-16420'. Added defrag call path guarded behind feature flag 'enable_defrag_on_alloc_fail'.

2025-02-15 — Priya Singh (PM): Notified affected customers about an engineering investigation and provided planned mitigations. Customer A requested priority rollout for their Dedicated cluster and asked for a rollback plan.

2025-02-16 — QA (Elena Ivanova): Ran canary tests on Hosted 10% traffic for 24h: no KV checksum errors and fragmentation score stayed within baseline. Noted 3% P99 latency increase in worst-case streaming scenarios; Diego to optimize staging blob allocation to avoid copy overhead.
2025-02-17 — Diego Ramirez: Addressed latency by reusing preallocated staging buffers for common frame sizes and reduced copy frequency. Pushed updated runtime build and opened PR for review.

2025-02-18 — Connor Lee: Code review complete. Left one follow-up to add a metric exposing rejected KV frame count and a small doc note for Private installers about the feature flag. Moving to In Review.
2025-02-18 — Maya Chen (SRE): Prepared Datadog dashboards and runbook entries for the hotfix; included steps to flip per-tenant 'disable_compaction' flag and verify OOM count returns to baseline.
remediation_steps: Enable per-tenant conservative allocator for Dedicated clusters with high churn
Flip 'disable_compaction' for affected Private installations if immediate rollback needed
Communicate ETA to customers and provide temporary capacity failover guidance
Run end-to-end KV checksum suite in CI and nightly long-tail scenario test
postmortem_action_items: Automate detection: add KV checksum monitor and pager rule
Improve autoscaler transparency: surface ongoing scale-in/scale-out events per tenant in console
Evaluate persistent staging-region for KV writes to reduce copy overheads
Scheduler/allocator work: triage longer-term compaction strategy to avoid in-place pointer reshuffles
Document operational playbook for Dedicated and Private teams for rapid config toggles
